task_row_model.query: A 68-year-old man presents with severe Clostridioides difficile infection and had a documented recurrence two months ago. What first-line oral antibiotic and duration should be used now, and what are evidence-based options to reduce further recurrence?

documents.content: Clinical guidance from an infectious diseases review recommends oral vancomycin 125 mg four times daily for 10 days or fidaxomicin 200 mg twice daily for 10 days as first-line therapy for initial and recurrent C. difficile infection, including severe presentations. Severe infection is operationalized in many protocols by leukocytosis >15,000/µL or a rise in creatinine to ≥1.5× baseline. For a first recurrence within eight weeks, the guidance advises fidaxomicin 200 mg twice daily for 10 days if available; if not feasible, a vancomycin taper/pulse regimen is recommended. The guideline includes historical context on C. difficile epidemiology and definitional boilerplate about severity criteria.

A randomized, double-blind trial comparing fidaxomicin 200 mg BID for 10 days with oral vancomycin 125 mg QID for 10 days in adults with C. difficile (n=548) found similar clinical cure rates (fidaxomicin 92% vs vancomycin 90%), but lower recurrence at 28 days with fidaxomicin: 15% versus 25% with vancomycin (absolute reduction 10%). The trial report emphasized that fidaxomicin’s narrower spectrum likely preserves gut microbiota, reducing relapse. Secondary analyses included subgroup statistics and speculative commentary on cost-effectiveness; unrelated appendices summarized antibiotic use trends in other infections and a brief unrelated case series of postoperative enterocolitis.
documents.reasoning_trace: Extracted trial outcomes (cure rates and recurrence rates) to quantify recurrence benefit of fidaxomicin versus vancomycin and noted similarity in initial clinical cure.

documents.content: Pharmacy guidance outlines a practical vancomycin taper/pulse schedule used for recurrent C. difficile: start with 125 mg PO four times daily for 10–14 days, then 125 mg twice daily for 7 days, then 125 mg once daily for 7 days, then 125 mg every 2–3 days for 2–8 weeks (pulse). The note discusses logistics, drug availability, and that metronidazole monotherapy is no longer recommended for severe disease. It also contains adjacent terminology explanations (colonization vs infection), a redundant restatement of the taper schedule, and a short unrelated vignette about fidaxomicin procurement challenges in some hospitals.

task_row_model.golden_answer: For severe C. difficile use oral vancomycin 125 mg PO four times daily for 10 days or fidaxomicin 200 mg PO twice daily for 10 days. For a first recurrence within eight weeks, use fidaxomicin 200 mg BID for 10 days if available; if not, give a vancomycin taper/pulse (125 mg QID 10–14 days, then 125 mg BID 7 days, then 125 mg daily 7 days, then 125 mg every 2–3 days for 2–8 weeks). Fidaxomicin reduced recurrence from 25% to 15% (absolute 10%).
